name: The Procter & Gamble Company

corporate_actions.event: Shailesh Jejurikar succeeded Jon Moeller as CEO; Moeller became Executive Chairman
Restructuring: up to ~7,000 non-manufacturing roles to be cut over two years; brand/category exits

geography.fx_notes: USD reporter; 'sales outside the US just over half' (S3) -> US just under 50% (not an exact disclosure). Greater China a high single-digit % historically (not verified this session). FX +2% on FY2026 sales (S1).

company_fcf.definition: Adjusted free cash flow (OCF - capex, excl. certain items)

lease.notes: US GAAP filer; operating lease cost within EBITDA; finance leases immaterial (not verified)

acquisitions.notes: No material acquisitions identified; P&G historically bolt-on only

management.senior_turnover_5y: Low and orderly: Taylor->Moeller (2021)->Jejurikar (2026), all internal
management.succession_notes: Planned internal succession; Moeller Executive Chair
management.guidance_record: Generally met/narrowed guidance; FY2026 organic +1% at low end of a slowing range

activists.name: Trian (Nelson Peltz) - historic
activists.company_response: Peltz added to board 2018; left 2021. No current activist identified

A.rationale: Highly recurring demand but one retailer >15%.

evidence: Pricing +9% in FY2023 with only -3% volume (S5)
B.rationale: Demonstrated pricing power and superiority-led share in most categories.

evidence: EBIT margin ~24% (PitchBook TTM) vs HPC peers high-teens/~20% (S6)
C.rationale: Scale in US retail, media and R&D translates into best-in-class margins.

evidence: Organic growth slowed to +1% FY2026; guided 1-3% (S1)
D.rationale: Mature, highly penetrated categories; runway limited to premiumisation/EM.

evidence: US just under half of sales (S3)
E.rationale: Two-region skew: US plus diversified international.

F.rationale: Experienced, stable management with credible track record.

evidence: Minimal M&A; steady dividends and buybacks (S3)
G.rationale: Disciplined capital allocation; buybacks at full valuations.

I4.rationale: Well placed to retain part of savings.

evidence: Tariff and commodity headwinds cited in FY2026/27 outlook (S1)
Core vs GAAP EPS differences mainly restructuring (S1)

ai.notes: No AI/data-centre or semis revenue (business mix).

sector_specific.volume_note: volume_pct = organic volume + mix; FY2022-FY2025 from recalled releases (confidence M)
sector_specific.private_label_risk: Low-medium: P&G superiority strategy holds share vs private label in US; private label gaining in diapers/tissue in downturns (INFERENCE)
sector_specific.top_customer_note: Walmart Inc. and affiliates ~16% of sales FY2024-2026 (S2)

gates.notes: G3 B: Walmart ~16% of sales (>15% single-customer rule). G1: low leverage (~1x). G7: negligible UK consumer exposure.

bull_points: Best-in-class margins and pricing power across daily-use categories (S5)
Orderly leadership succession; productivity programme supports EPS
Low leverage and long dividend record
bear_points: Organic growth slowed to +1% with flat volume in FY2026; guidance 1-3% (S1)
Walmart dependence (~16%) and retailer/private-label pressure in US (S2)
Growth FY2022-24 was price-driven; US consumer slowdown and tariffs
thesis_breakers: Walmart share of sales above 20% or loss of category share in US
